lyrics: The first sound wasn't a doctor's slap.
It was the closing latch of a poverty
trap. The first light wasn't the morning sun.
It was the glare of a race that was already
run.
They don't check
your eyes, they don't check your soul. They just run your
address through a market control. You're a risk
assessment, a value proposition. A pre-approved slide
into grim attrition.
Just a number
stamped on a county   file. With your whole life
story in the fine-print   style. They don't use no
iron, they don't use no   flame. But you're branded at
birth by the zip code's name.
Your mother whispers
a prayer for you,   son. Hopes you'll be the
one, yeah, the lucky   one. But the streets are
wired and the deck is   stacked. There ain't no road
forward, ain't no turnin' back.
Some kids get a   cradle, some kids get a
map. You get a consumer   profile and a bootstrap
snap. They'll tell you to pull, but the boot's nailed
down. In this forgotten   corner
of a forgotten town.
Just a number   stamped on a county
file. With your whole life   story in the fine-print
style. They don't use no   iron, they don't use no
flame. But you're branded at   birth by the zip
code's name.
Branded like a   steer on the day you
were born. Fenced in the   pasture 'til
your spirit's torn. Marked as the   property of circumstance.
Never given half a   chance,
not a goddamn glance.
Just a number stamped on a county
file. With your whole life   story in the fine-print
style. They don't use no   iron, they don't use no
flame. But you're branded at   birth by the zip
code's name.
Yeah, branded at   birth by the
zip code's name.
